general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **EU-Mercosur Trade Deal:** EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed the EU-Mercosur Trade Agreement in Brussels on November 23, 2026. The treaty eliminates tariffs on 91% of goods and mandates binding adherence to the Paris Agreement for all signatories. Markets in São Paulo and Frankfurt rose by 1.2% immediately following the announcement. This creates one of the world's largest free-trade zones, strategically reducing European reliance on Chinese industrial imports. Reuters

• **Geneva AI Convention:** US Secretary of State Antony Blinken and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi ratified the Geneva Convention on Autonomous Weapons Systems on November 23, 2026, with support from 114 nations. The treaty prohibits the deployment of lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS) that operate without direct human authorization. The UN Security Council established a monitoring body in Vienna to conduct quarterly audits of military AI laboratories. This prevents a fully automated arms race and establishes the first global legal framework for the regulation of artificial general intelligence. Associated Press

• **Bank of Japan Interest Rates:** Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda raised the short-term interest rate to 1.5% on November 23, 2026, the highest level since 2008. The decision followed a report showing Japan's core inflation remained at 3.2% for the third consecutive month. The Yen strengthened by 2.4% against the US Dollar, reaching a rate of 132 JPY/USD. This shift ends decades of ultra-loose monetary policy and may trigger a massive repatriation of Japanese capital from US Treasury bonds. Financial Times

• **Sahel Green Infrastructure Fund:** The African Union and the World Bank announced a $45 billion "Green Infrastructure Fund" on November 23, 2026, to construct solar grids across the Sahel. The project targets the provision of electricity to 120 million people in Niger, Mali, and Chad by 2030. Five multinational consortia from India and the EU submitted bids for the initial $10 billion phase within 12 hours of the announcement. Stabilizing energy access in the Sahel is a strategic effort to curb climate-driven migration and economic collapse in North Africa. Al Jazeera

Why it matters: A simultaneous shift toward institutional stability in AI, global trade, and monetary policy suggests a transition toward a more regulated, multipolar economic order.
